 Proposed SNAP change could cut benefits for millions 
 Local food banks like Feeding the Gulf Coast say the proposal could lead to more people reaching out for help. By Daeshen Smith Published : Nov. 16, 2026 at 4:59 PM CST | Updated : 12 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google MOBILE, Ala. ( WALA ) - A proposed change could lead to millions of people losing access to SNAP benefits.
 The proposal would cut back broad-based categorical eligibility. The tool allows states to use Temporary Assistance for Needy Families benefits, such as childcare or workforce training, to qualify households for SNAP without applying the standard income eligibility limit. If the proposal moves forward, people receiving TANF services would no longer automatically qualify.
 Michael Ledger, president and CEO of Feeding the Gulf Coast, said the change, along with other proposed changes, would affect neighbors.
 “This tool along with other proposed changes could make a big difference for neighbors and unfortunately they won’t be good ones,” Ledger said.
 H.R. 1 passed last year and affected SNAP benefits for about 5.5 million people, according to the Food Research and Action Center. The new proposal would result in about 6.3 million additional people losing their benefits.
 Local food banks like Feeding the Gulf Coast say the proposal could lead to more people reaching out for help.
 Ledger said the organization distributed 45 million pounds of food last year and is on track to match that this year. He said filling the gap would be a challenge.
 “For every meal we provide, SNAP provides nine and there’s no way we could scale to that level. We worked hard to reach folks during the hurricane and the government shutdown last year so we can scale up a little but it’s a different ball game when you talk about nine-fold,” Ledger said.
 Ledger said nearly 400,000 people in the organization’s service area struggle to put food on the table. He said the proposal could slow people down while they try to get back on their feet.
 “The other misunderstanding is that folks are on these programs for long long periods of time. What we know is so many our families with children, seniors, disabled. Many families face crisis. This helps families and individuals through crisis so they can stay on their feet and get back to normal sooner,” Ledger said.
 Ledger said the organization has been reaching out to local, state and federal legislators to try to keep the proposal from moving forward.
 Written comments about the proposal are being accepted until Dec. 10. If you want more information or to leave a comment you can do so here .
